pamphlet_excerpts: Life and Times of Lord: Thedivide between rich and poor was widening, and most familieswere poor or close (p. 9).
Life and Times of Lord Principle 2: As people migrated to dirty, overcrowdedcities, they were more likely to become sick and less likely to beable to enjoy nature or get physical exercise (p. 9).
Life and Times of Lord Principle 3: In fact, when Britain went to war in 1899, more than half the men whovolunteered for the army weren't fit enough to fight (p. 9).
Life and Times of Lord Principle 4: Children on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean suffered right along with their parents (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Life and Times of Lord): Beyond the YMCA and some church-based programs, few organized activities or sportsleagues were available for them toenjoy (p. 9).
Step 2 (Life and Times of Lord): Even worse, at least 1.7 million American children under the age of 16 worked full time, sometimes workingas many as 12 hours a day in factories (p. 9).
Step 3 (Life and Times of Lord): Many adults grew deeply concernedabout the problems of English and Child laborer, circa early 20th century American children (p. 9).
Step 4 (Life and Times of Lord): Among them were Robert Baden-Powell, Ernest Thompson Seton, and Daniel Carter Beard (p. 9).

pamphlet_excerpts: Scouting's Programs Have Developed: In 1935, the BSA created a program called Explorer Scouts asone option in Senior Scouting (p. 38).
Scouting's Programs Have Developed Principle 2: It offered to older Boy Scouts a land-based alternative to Sea Scouting (p. 38).
Scouting's Programs Have Developed Principle 3: Explorer Scouts initially wore the same uniform as Boy Scouts, although it featured an "Explorer Scout, BSA" stripover the right pocket (p. 38).
Scouting's Programs Have Developed Principle 4: In the 1940s, a forest-green uniform wasintroduced, and Explorer Scout units began to be called postsinstead of troops (p. 38).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): Explorer Scouts got their own advancement programin 1944 (p. 38).
Step 2 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): The four ranks, Apprentice, Woodsman, Frontiersman, and Ranger, corresponded to the four ranksin Sea Scouting (p. 38).
Step 3 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): In 1949, Explorer Scoutsbecame simply Explorers, and the program's focus wasexpanded to include socialactivities, service opportunities (p. 38).
Step 4 (Scouting's Programs Have Developed): More and more, posts began to specialize in specific careersor hobbies (p. 38).

requirements.lead_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to Scouting. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. With permission of your parent or guardian, your research methods may include an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to serve as a Scouting volunteer. Research any training needed, expenses, and how you could serve as a unit, district, council, regional, or national volunteer. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.
